bottlenecks.reading: Advanced packaging (CoWoS) is the tightest AI bottleneck: a supply-demand gap of ~20% reportedly narrowing to ~10% by end-2026; TSMC reportedly plans to roughly double capacity by 2028 and seeks ~20% CoWoS price rises. Analyst/press estimates, not TSMC guidance.

Leading-edge wafers are concentrated: TSMC held 72.5% of 2Q26 foundry revenue (Samsung 5.9%, SMIC 5.4%); 20-F says 3/5/7nm were 24%/36%/14% of 2025 wafer revenue (74% advanced). No rival has yet shown external volume at comparable nodes.
Pricing power signal: wafer prices reportedly rising 3-6% from Jan 2027 with 2nm/3nm steepest (press report of TrendForce, unconfirmed by TSMC).

Share risk hypothesis: Intel 18A/14A could win some external AI/PC volume from 2H26-2028 (Tesla 14A reported; Apple reports are analyst claims). Intel external foundry revenue is only $293M in 2Q26 vs TSMC ~$40.2B.

dc CALL 2026-10-15 Q3 2026 earnings call (CFO Wendell Huang, Chairman/CEO C.C. Wei); transcript copy from Motley Fool (syndicated from the issuer call), AV transcript not used (AV daily limit exhausted today, per owner).
dc MGMT Q3: revenue US$46.7bn above the high end of guidance; gross margin down 1.3pts q/q to 66.4% 'primarily due to margin dilution from 2nm ramp' (dc_call_q3_2026).

dc MGMT Q4 guide: gross margin to fall about 0.4pt at midpoint to 66% on continued steep 2nm ramp plus overseas fab dilution, partly offset by cost improvement and across-node capacity optimization; revenue midpoint +14% q/q and +58% y/y in US dollars.
dc MGMT overseas fabs: gross margin dilution now 'closer to 2%'; management expects it to widen to 3-4% in the next few years as more U.S. fabs ramp.

dc MGMT CAPEX: 2026 capital budget US$60-64bn (the 20-F of 2026-04-16 said US$52-56bn; the range was raised earlier in 2026, date not found in the sources read, 'reiterated' on the Q3 call); capex 2026-2028 'significantly higher than the past three years'; Q3 capex US$13.8bn. Tool price inflation 'is real'.

dc MGMT DEMAND: 'demand is extremely robust ... gap between demand and supply still quite big'; AI accelerator CAGR previously guided to mid-to-high 50s% for 2024-2029, CEO: 'it probably will be higher' (a statement, not a new numeric guide). Agentic-AI CPUs and networking add silicon demand.
dc MGMT CAUTION: consumer and price-sensitive end markets are being challenged by rising component prices and macro uncertainty; management is 'being prudent' in planning for 2027.

dc MGMT CAPACITY: nearly 20 fabs in progress (13 leading-edge and advanced-packaging fabs in Taiwan, 5-6 overseas). N2 in high-volume production since Q4 2025; N2-family annual capacity to more than double in 2027; A14 risk production 2027, volume 2028. Three new N3 fabs added: Tainan fab volume 1H27, an additional Tainan fab 1H28, Arizona fab 2 volume 3Q27 (ahead of schedule), Japan fab 2 on 3nm in 2028. High NA EUV planned for 2030.

dc MGMT U.S.: evaluating Texas as another U.S. site and discussing capacity with a customer's 'Terafab' project; any fab 'has to be run by TSMC'; no solid conclusion yet. Long-term profitability: 'no ceiling ... but a dramatic increase will not happen overnight'.
dc MGMT dividend: committed to a sustainable and steadily increasing cash dividend per share; board approved NT$7.00 for Q2 2026 (ex-dividend 2026-12-10, payable 2027-01-07) per the presentation.

dc FACT Q3 2026 vs Q3 2025: revenue +50.9% (NT$), +41.2% (US$); gross margin 66.4% vs 59.5%; operating margin 58.7% vs 50.6%; net income +68.7%; non-operating items NT$34.6bn vs NT$95.8bn in Q2 (net income margin 51.1%). Platform mix Q3: HPC 68% (+22% q/q), smartphone 21% (+10%), IoT 4% (+5%), automotive 4% (+23%), DCE 1% (-12%).

dc FACT cash and marketable securities NT$4.02tn (US$126bn) against long-term interest-bearing debt NT$818bn (current portion of bonds/loans rose NT$46bn q/q and is NOT in this long-term line); investments and others +NT$167.6bn in the cash walk; the cash walk's ending balance (NT$3.62tn) is cash only, a different line from cash and marketable securities.

dc FACT FY2025 concentration (20-F note on major customers): Customer A 19% (12% in 2024), Customer B 17% (22% in 2024, 25% in 2023); ten largest customers 78% of net revenue in 2025 (76% in 2024, 70% in 2023) per Item 3; the 20-F note on credit risk gives 93% for the ten largest in receivables terms (not revenue). Customers are unnamed in the filing; naming them would be an inference.

dc FACT FY2025 contractual obligations (20-F Item 5): capital and other purchase obligations NT$1.53tn, of which NT$1.22tn due within one year; long-term debt NT$1.23tn contractual; no formal backlog or RPO is disclosed by TSMC.

dc FACT FY2025 platform revenue (20-F Item 4): HPC NT$2,192.9bn (58%), smartphone NT$1,110.8bn (29%), IoT NT$191.0bn (5%), automotive NT$186.7bn (5%), DCE NT$48.0bn (1%), others NT$79.6bn (2%); total NT$3,809.1bn; wafer fabrication about 86% of net revenue.
dc FACT segment profit: TSMC reports one operating segment; there is no operating income by platform (operating_income left null).
dc RISK Customer concentration: ten largest customers 78% of 2025 revenue, two largest 19% and 17% (20-F Item 3.D, risks relating to our business).

dc RISK Cyclicality and fixed costs: semiconductor and electronics are cyclical, most capacity is owned so a large share of cost is fixed and margins fall when utilization drops (20-F Item 3.D, cyclical industry risk factor).

dc RISK Geopolitics, tariffs and export controls: U.S. Section 232 25% tariff on certain semiconductor items from Dec 2025 with offsets unclear, IEEPA tariffs struck down Feb 2026 with a replacement Section 122 tariff, U.S. export controls (October Rules) on advanced chips to China (20-F Item 3.D, lines about 505-565 of the text).

dc RISK Technology leadership and AI concentration: must keep node leadership (N2, A14) and meet a faster AI customer cadence; losing the edge would erode share (20-F Item 3.D, technological leader risk factor).

dc RISK Capacity expansion and overseas execution: about 20 fabs under construction, capex US$60-64bn in 2026, overseas fab margin dilution 2% widening to 3-4%, tool price inflation, utilities/land constraints (20-F Item 3.D; Q3 2026 call).

dc RISK Demand/ASP of end markets: HPC/AI, smartphone, IoT, automotive and DCE demand can fall with component shortages, power supply constraints or macro; consumer end markets already weak per Q3 call (20-F Item 3.D; call).

dc RISK Currency: results and guidance depend on the USD/NTD rate (Q4 guide assumes 31.8; Q3 average 31.98; 29.91 in Q3 2025); a stronger NT dollar lowers NT$ margins (20-F Item 11; guidance footnote).

mc EXPOSURE Taiwan concentration: 20-F risk factor says the majority of principal production facilities and executive officers are in the R.O.C.; 80% of noncurrent assets are in Taiwan; fabs per Item 4: Taiwan (Central and Southern Science Parks), 2 in the US (Arizona, Washington State), 1 Shanghai, 1 Nanjing, 1 Japan (Kumamoto). Named perils: military conflict/outbreak of war, earthquakes (losses NT$3.0bn Q2 2024 and NT$5.3bn Q1 2025 net of insurance), typhoon, drought, electricity and water shortage. Size: the evidenced exposure is ~80% of long-lived assets; revenue exposure to a Taiwan production outage is effectively the Taiwan-fabbed share of wafers, which the filing does not disclose (gap, hypothesis-sized). [pf_10k_20260416]

mc EXPOSURE US export controls (China): Oct 2022/Oct 2023/Jan 2025 EAR rules; license may be needed for 16nm-and-below shipments to specified destinations. Nanjing fab (Fab 16) lost its VEU in Dec 2025 and now runs on an annual US export license, no assurance of renewal; the company says results have not been materially affected so far. China-HQ customers were 9% of FY2025 revenue (NT$327.5bn) and China noncurrent assets 1.7% (NT$65.0bn), which bounds the sized exposure; a Nanjing share of ~2.4% of 2024 revenue appears in one press lead only (unconfirmed). Chinese blocking statute (Jan 2021) is a counter-risk. [pf_10k_20260416; mc_press_nanjing]

mc EXPOSURE US tariffs: 20-F states IEEPA tariffs were declared unlawful by the Supreme Court in Feb 2026, replaced by a Section 122 tariff; USTR opened two Section 301 investigations (March 2026) including Taiwan; Section 232 on semiconductors concluded Dec 2025 with a 25% ad valorem tariff on certain advanced computing chips meeting performance thresholds unless imported for designated US use, with a signal of broader tariffs and an offset program; Jan 2026 US-Taiwan agreement caps reciprocal rate at 15% and grants preferential Section 232 treatment to Taiwanese producers investing in US capacity, details unclear after the court ruling. Exposed base: North America customers are 75% of revenue, but wafers are mostly imported by customers/ODMs, so the incidence on TSMC is mainly demand and price negotiation, not a direct duty (hypothesis; share not disclosed). Press lead: investment pledge of $250bn plus $250bn credit guarantees and a quota multiple of planned US capacity that is duty-free during construction (sources disagree on 1.5x vs 2.5x; check Commerce text). [pf_10k_20260416; mc_press_232_taiwan; mc_press_232_proc]

mc EXPOSURE Customer concentration with US export-policy overlap: FY2025 customers above 10%: Customer A 19% (NT$726,974m), Customer B 17% (NT$645,179m); in 2024 A 12% and B 22%. mc EXPOSURE Overseas expansion cost and funding: Arizona direct funding agreement with the US Dept of Commerce of up to US$6.6bn plus up to US$5bn government loans (Nov 2024); 2026 capex guidance raised to US$60-64bn (press, from the Oct 2026 call, from US$52-56bn); overseas fabs carry cost and tariff-offset implications for margin (hypothesis, not sized here). market_direction.reading: The market TSMC serves is growing fast and tilting to AI/HPC: HPC rose from 58% of FY2025 revenue (NT$2,192.9bn) to 68% in Q3 2026 (+22% q/q); FY2026 revenue growth is guided at about 44% in US$ and Q4 2026 at US$52.3-54.3bn (+58% y/y at midpoint). Management previously guided AI accelerator revenue CAGR of mid-to-high 50s% for 2024-2029 and said on the Q3 call it 'probably will be higher' (a statement, not a new numeric guide); it also flagged consumer/price-sensitive end markets as challenged and 'prudent' planning for 2027. Industry: top-10 foundry revenue hit a record US$53.49bn in 2Q26 (TrendForce).

bottleneck_potential.reading: TSMC is the bottleneck for leading-edge logic: 79% of Q3 2026 wafer revenue is 7nm and below (N2 8%, N3 33%, N5 28%), N2 in volume since Q4 2025 with N2-family capacity to more than double in 2027 and A14 volume in 2028; management says the demand-supply gap is 'still quite big'. Advanced packaging (CoWoS) is the tightest AI constraint: an estimated ~20% supply-demand gap narrowing to ~10% by end-2026 as TSMC adds capacity (TrendForce estimate, not TSMC guidance). Capacity is added mainly by TSMC itself (nearly 20 fabs in progress, 2026 capex US$60-64bn); no rival shows external leading-edge volume yet, so the position looks durable for at least the 2027-2028 node cycle; the narrowing CoWoS gap means the packaging tightness itself is temporary.

share_trajectory.reading: TSMC is holding or gaining share on numbers: 72.5% of 2Q26 foundry revenue vs 72.3% in 1Q26 (TrendForce); Samsung Foundry fell from 6.5% to 5.9%; SMIC rose from 5.1% to 5.4% (mature/domestic China nodes); UMC 3.9%; GlobalFoundries ~4% of pure foundry (Counterpoint, different basis). Intel's external foundry revenue was US$293M in 2Q26, under 1% of TSMC's ~US$40.2bn quarter. Only two quarters of share data were read, so the trend is short.

competitive_position.reading: Stronger than every named competitor. Vs Samsung Foundry (the only other 3nm/2nm GAA maker): 72.5% vs 5.9% share and falling for Samsung. Vs Intel Foundry: Intel FY2025 revenue -0.5%, gross margin 34.8%, operating margin -4.2% vs TSMC FY2025 gross margin ~59.9% and operating margin ~50.8%, Q3 2026 66.4%/58.7%; Intel 18A yields are improving (reported 7-8% monthly) but external revenue is tiny. Vs SMIC, UMC, GlobalFoundries: they compete in mature/specialty nodes, while 79% of TSMC's wafer revenue is 7nm and below. TSMC's ROIC ~53% (incremental ~61%) shows the economics behind the position.

threats.reading: (1) Customer concentration/in-sourcing of demand: two unnamed customers were 19% and 17% of FY2025 revenue and the ten largest 78% (up from 70% in 2023); an AI-capex pullback at them hits about a third of revenue. (2) Geopolitics: ~80% of noncurrent assets (NT$3.10tn of NT$3.88tn) are in Taiwan; US export controls (Nanjing fab on an annual license; China-HQ customers 9% of FY2025 revenue) and US Section 232 tariffs (25% on certain advanced chips, Taiwan deal caps reciprocal rate at 15%). (3) New entrant: Intel 18A/14A external foundry (hypothesis that it wins material volume; today US$293M a quarter). (4) Cost: overseas fab gross-margin dilution ~2% now, guided to widen to 3-4%. (5) Cyclicality: mostly fixed costs, margins fall when utilization drops (FY2023 revenue -4.5%).

bear.event_he: הלקוחות הגדולים (שני הגדולים = 36% מההכנסות, עשרת הגדולים = 78%) מקצצים הזמנות לשבבי בינה מלאכותית ב-2027-2028 אחרי גל ההשקעות.
מחזור ירידה בתעשייה כמו ב-2023 (הכנסות -4.5%), והפעם חד יותר כי מחשוב-על הוא 68% מההכנסות.
הרווחיות נשחקת: המפעלים בארה"ב וביפן מורידים 3-4 נקודות מהרווח הגולמי, ומחירי הציוד עולים.
מתיחות סביב טייוואן או מכסים אמריקאיים (סעיף 232) פוגעים בייצור או במחיר: 80% מהנכסים הקבועים בטייוואן.
אינטל או סמסונג זוכות בלקוח גדול לייצור מתקדם ומקטינות את הנתח של TSMC.

base.event_he: רבעון רביעי 2026 בטווח ההנחיה (52.3-54.3 מיליארד דולר) או מעליו, כמו בשבעת הרבעונים האחרונים; צמיחה של כ-44% בדולר ב-2026.
כושר הייצור ב-2 ננומטר יותר מוכפל ב-2027 ושלושה מפעלי 3 ננומטר חדשים נכנסים (טאינאן 2027, אריזונה רבעון שלישי 2027).
הנתח בשוק הייצור נשאר מעל 70% והביקוש עדיין גבוה מההיצע.
ההשקעות עולות ל-60-64 מיליארד דולר ב-2026 ויותר ב-2027-2028, ממומנות מהתזרים בלי דילול.

bull.event_he: קצב ההכנסות מבינה מלאכותית עולה על התחזית של צמיחה שנתית של 55%-60% עד 2029, כפי שהמנכ"ל רמז ('כנראה יותר').
הרווח התפעולי נשאר סביב 57%, ברמת ההנחיה לרבעון הרביעי 2026.
העלאות מחירי פרוסות של 3%-6% מינואר 2027 (במיוחד 2 ו-3 ננומטר) מחזיקות.
A14 נכנס לייצור המוני ב-2028 בזמן, והמתחרים (אינטל 18A/14A, סמסונג) לא סוגרים את הפער.

growth_anchor.reason: Growth of FY2027 over FY2026 = NT$5,593.7bn (drivers.current_year_revenue: 9M reported + Q4 guide). No FY2027 guidance or attributed consensus. The Q4 2026 guide annualized (NT$6,780bn, US$213bn) is already about 21% above FY2026, so flat quarters from Q4 give +21%. Base +27% (FY2027 about NT$7.10tn, US$223bn): only about 1-2% average sequential growth through 2027 as N2-family capacity more than doubles and management says demand still exceeds supply; management calls itself prudent on 2027 and gives no number, so this stays the most likely path but without a guide. Bull +38%: FY2026-like momentum (+44%) slightly faded. Bear -4.5%: an explicit down year sized to the FY2023 decline (-4.5% y/y). Against the exit run rate it is sharper than 2023: the average 2027 quarter falls about 21% below the Q4 2026 guided level (in 2023 the average quarter was about 14% below Q4 2022), because HPC is now 68% of revenue and the two largest customers 36%, so an AI-capex digestion hits a larger share at once.

growth.reason: FY2027-FY2030 on the FY2026 base NT$5,593.7bn (9M reported + Q4 guide). Base fades from +27% toward the low teens as the AI accelerator CAGR management cited (mid-to-high 50s % 2024-2029 for that line) becomes a larger share and capex 2026-2028 'significantly higher' adds N3/N2/A14 capacity (A14 volume 2028). Bull keeps capacity-limited growth longer. Bear: the digestion down year in 2027 (-4.5%, the FY2023 size, sharper than 2023 against the exit run rate), then a flat 2028 while the new 2026-2028 capacity is underused (no AI-led rebound like 2024's), then a single-digit recovery.

mature_margin.reason: Operating margin. Bear 44%: the FY2019-FY2024 average (43.7%) when utilization and pricing revert. Base 52%: FY2025's 50.8% plus the structural gain of a 72% share and N2 pricing, less the overseas dilution management says widens from ~2 to 3-4 points; below today's 58.7% peak. Bull 57%: the Q4 2026 guided range (56.5-58.5%) held.

tax_rate.reason: FY2025 effective tax rate 17.0% (income tax NT$346.5bn over pre-tax NT$2,041.7bn, 20-F); same in every scenario: no evidence of a scenario-dependent rate.

current_year_revenue.reason: FY2026 = reported Q1-Q3 2026 (NT$3,898.7bn) + the Q4 2026 revenue guide midpoint US$53.3bn at the guided 31.8 NT$/US$ (NT$1,694.9bn) = NT$5,593.7bn (US$175.9bn, consistent with the 'around 44%' US$ growth guide). Track record (7/7 beats, ratio about 1.024) not applied: the Q4 guide is in US$, so it cannot be the remainder item; applying it to Q4 only would add about NT$40bn (+0.7%).

bear.reason_he: אם לקוחות הבינה המלאכותית עוצרים קניות כמו ב-2023 (אז התשואה על ההון ירדה לשפל של כ-45% והרווחיות התפעולית ל-42.6%), והמפעלים בחו"ל מורידים עוד עד 4 נקודות רווחיות, ההון המושקע מחזיר כ-40% (45% כפול 38.6 חלקי 42.6), ולכן המכפיל נמוך יותר. ייקור הציוד לא מכומת.

base.reason_he: החברה מרוויחה היום כ-53% על ההון המושקע (ותשואה להון 45.5% ברבעון 3 של 2026), ובשלוש השנים האחרונות כ-61% על ההון החדש; ניקינו את השיא ואת פגיעת המפעלים בחו"ל (כ-2-3 נקודות רווחיות) ולקחנו 35%, ולכן מכפיל גבוה מוצדק שיורד כשהצמיחה מאטה. מוניטין זניח, אינו משנה.

bull.reason_he: אם 2 ננומטר (כבר 8% מהכנסות הוופלים ברבעון 3) והביקוש לבינה מלאכותית שומרים על רווחיות גולמית של כ-66% גם עם המפעלים בחו"ל, ההון החדש מחזיר כ-50%, קרוב לתשואה של השנים האחרונות; זה עוד לא הוכח על המפעלים החדשים.

key_risk.reading_he: הסיכון המרכזי: TSMC תלויה בגל השקעות הבינה המלאכותית של מעט לקוחות (עשרת הגדולים 78% מההכנסות, מחשוב-על 68%) בזמן שהרווחיות בשיא (58.7%) וההשקעות במפעלים חדשים עולות; האטה אצל הלקוחות האלה תפגע ברווח מהר, כי רוב העלויות קבועות. מעל זה עומד סיכון טייוואן (80% מהנכסים).

moat.note: Process-technology and scale moat: 72.5% foundry share vs Samsung 5.9% and Intel external foundry US$293M/quarter; 79% of wafer revenue at 7nm and below; ROIC ~53% with incremental ROIC ~61%, far above an ~8% cost of capital, sustained since 2019 (no fade toward the cost of capital in the data).

pricing_power.note: Gross margin rose from 46% (FY2019) and 56.1% (FY2024) to 59.9% (FY2025) and 66.4% (Q3 2026), guided 65-67% for Q4 2026 despite 2nm ramp and overseas dilution. Reported 2027 wafer price rises of 3-6% and CoWoS price rises are press/analyst claims (hypothesis, moves nothing).

customer_concentration.note: High concentration: Customer A 19% (12% in 2024), Customer B 17% (22% in 2024); ten largest 78% of FY2025 revenue. Customers are unnamed in the filing.

market_size.note: FY2026 revenue guided ~+44% in US$; HPC 68% of revenue; management's AI accelerator CAGR guide of mid-to-high 50s% for 2024-2029 (management expectation); industry foundry revenue at a record US$53.49bn in 2Q26.

competition.note: TSMC's competitive standing is strong: Samsung losing share (6.5% to 5.9%), Intel loss-making with tiny external foundry revenue, SMIC/UMC/GlobalFoundries mostly in mature nodes. Intel 18A/14A is the one named challenger to watch.

management.note: Promises vs delivery: revenue beat the guided midpoint in 7 of 7 quarters from Q1 2025 to Q3 2026 (mean actual/guided midpoint 1.024); Q3 2026 US$46.72bn vs guidance US$44.6-45.8bn.

capital_allocation.note: Heavy reinvestment at high returns (incremental ROIC ~61%): FY2025 capex NT$1.27tn funded from CFO NT$2.27tn; dividends rose to NT$466.8bn from NT$363.1bn; SBC negligible (NT$1.2bn) and the share count flat (~25.93bn). Watch: capex rising to US$60-64bn in 2026 and higher in 2027-2028, with lower-return overseas fabs (gross margin dilution 2% widening to 3-4%) partly driven by politics.

regulation.note: Exposed to US export controls (Nanjing on an annual license, China-HQ customers 9% of revenue) and Section 232 tariffs, mitigated by the Jan 2026 US-Taiwan deal and US investment (Arizona); company says results not materially affected so far.

technology_ai.note: N2 in high-volume production since Q4 2025 and already 8% of wafer revenue in Q3 2026; A14 risk production 2027, volume 2028; Intel 18A still ramping yields; AI is the main growth driver (HPC 68%).

geopolitics.note: About 80% of noncurrent assets in Taiwan; the 20-F names military conflict, earthquakes, power and water shortages; a customer (Anthropic S-1, secondary report) flags Taiwan concentration as a supply risk. Not sizable as a probability; the revenue share at risk in a Taiwan outage is not disclosed.

cyclical.reason: The 20-F names the semiconductor cycle and FY2023 revenue fell 4.5%, but TSMC's share keeps rising (72.5% of 2Q26 foundry revenue), growth is driven by value per wafer (shipments +9.6% y/y vs revenue +51%) and node leadership; the cycle is carried as an explicit 2028 down year in the bear instead of normalizing today's revenue to a trend.
